fix.notes: The fix is a one-liner matching the existing pattern in store_image(). aiohttp.ClientResponseError is a subclass of aiohttp.ClientError so no changes to the except clause were needed. No other issues discovered.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`store_async` in `shared/fetch_tools.py` silently ignored HTTP 4xx/5xx error responses from Scryfall when downloading images. It would write the error response body to disk as though it were a valid image, while the synchronous `store_image` already called `response.raise_for_status()` to detect these failures.

## What changed

Added `response.raise_for_status()` immediately after `response = await aios.get(url)` in `store_async` (line 178). `aiohttp.ClientResponseError` — raised by `raise_for_status()` on 4xx/5xx responses — is a subclass of `aiohttp.ClientError`, which is already caught by the existing `except` clause and converted to `FetchException`.

Also added `test_store_async_raises_on_4xx` to `shared/fetch_tools_test.py`, mirroring the existing `test_store_image_rejects_http_error` test for the sync path.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks passed)
- `uv run --frozen pytest shared/fetch_tools_test.py -v` — 6 passed, including the new async test

Fixes #5703
fix.pr_title: Raise FetchException on 4xx responses in store_async (#5703)

evidence.detail: store_async does not call response.raise_for_status(); a Scryfall 4xx error body is silently written to the output file path
Synchronous store_image() does call response.raise_for_status() — inconsistency confirms the omission in store_async is unintentional
Exception handler catches aiohttp.ClientError which is the parent of aiohttp.ClientResponseError (raised by raise_for_status) — adding one line is safe and self-contained

This mirrors the existing pattern in store_image(). aiohttp.ClientResponseError is a subclass of aiohttp.ClientError so the existing except clause will convert it to FetchException automatically.
triage.notes: Without the fix, failed downloads leave small (<1000 byte) error-JSON files on disk; acceptable_file() already prevents them from being used, so behavior is self-healing but error diagnosis is harder and disk accumulates stale files.
